paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: loyalty to the LORD doesn't depend on how impressive the voice is. Moses says a prophet's sign can come true, and the LORD still says don't listen if he pushes other gods (Deuteronomy 13:1-3). I think that's wild, because we'd all say, "Well, he got the sign right!" But Moses says the LORD is testing Israel "to find out whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your soul" (Deuteronomy 13:3).

Then Moses makes it personal, and I think this part hurts: the pull toward other gods can come from a brother, a son or daughter, the wife you embrace, or your closest friend (Deuteronomy 13:6). Moses says the one who tries to turn them away is trying to pull them from the LORD, who "brought you out of the land of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 13:10). It's the same with a whole city: Moses says to inquire, investigate and interrogate thoroughly before anything happens (Deuteronomy 13:14). This is a heavy passage, so I'm not going to joke about the judgments in it.

So what does it mean for you, baker? The answer to a persuasive voice, even a loved one's, is the LORD's own words: "You are to follow the LORD your God and fear Him. Keep His commandments and listen to His voice; serve Him and hold fast to Him" (Deuteronomy 13:4). HOLD FAST, friend, because Moses says the LORD wants hearts that stay with Him when the sign is dazzling and when the voice is someone dear. And the story isn't over, because Moses is NOT done preaching yet.
